text:
emily: customer reports invoice shows ~3.2k tokens charged but dashboard and per-request logs show ~2.1k. they say this only happens on streaming endpoints when the client reconnects mid-generation. ledger id: L-43811. session id: s-9c2f. can eng take a look?

sam (acme-inc): yep, happened twice yesterday. network blip, client reconnected within 1s and we got two 'final' messages in the UI. dashboard counts looked fine during the session. invoice spike appeared later. attaching raw SSE snippet below.

sam (acme-inc): ```
event: chunk
data: {"token_count":1024,"text":"..."}

event: chunk
data: {"token_count":900,"text":"..."}

event: final
data: {"final":true,"trailer_tokens":250,"id":"stream-7f"}

# client reconnects (network)
event: chunk
data: {"token_count":0,"text":""}

event: final
data: {"final":true,"trailer_tokens":250,"id":"stream-7f"}
```

emily: logs show two final/trailer emissions with the same id after reconnect. dashboard aggregation seems to de-duplicate by request id, but billing metering ledger captured both entries.

anita: curious — do we have the raw metering events for L-43811? metering pipeline should coalesce final/trailer tokens by event id, but looks like the dedupe key wasn't populated on the second emission (reconnect path).

kevin: tagging billing team. if ledger counted both trailers we need a credit. who owns the dedupe key generation?

anita: it should be set in runtime when we emit the trailer: we add event_id = request_id + "-trailer". if client reconnect goes through the passthrough path, request_id sometimes becomes ephemeral (we reassign a reconnect id). that would explain why two different dedupe keys were generated but both had same trailer_tokens.

metering-bot: METRIC-LOG L-43811: received_meter_event {"event_type":"trailer","tokens":250,"dedupe_key":"stream-7f-trailer-v1"} at 2026-11-03T01:12:23Z
metering-bot: METRIC-LOG L-43811: received_meter_event {"event_type":"trailer","tokens":250,"dedupe_key":"stream-7f-reconn-9a-trailer-v1"} at 2026-11-03T01:12:24Z

kevin: ok that matches — two distinct dedupe_key values => double charge. action items: (1) refund/credit invoice for L-43811 for 250 tokens x2 (excess 250) pending verification, (2) engineering patch to ensure reconnect path preserves original trailer dedupe_key, (3) add an integration test that simulates client reconnect within 0-2s and asserts single metering event.

anita: provisional patch: on reconnect, if we detect a previous stream with matching stream-id header, propagate original request_id to the reconnect context. simple guard: if stream-id header present, use cached request_id. also will add defensive dedupe on the metering side: collapse trailer events within 5s window by stream-id+final-id. i'll open PR.

emily: can you also drop the raw invoice payload to billing so they can generate a credit? i've attached the invoice id in the thread, invoice INV-2026-11-03-ACME.

kevin: filing credit ticket now. tagging @finance. putting hold on auto-pay until resolved. will follow up with credit reference CR-7521.

sam (acme-inc): thanks — appreciate the fast turnaround. FYI our client uses a short reconnect TTL intentionally to avoid long stalls; any workaround we can recommend in the meantime?

anita: short-term: on client side, debounce reconnects for 2s OR include stream-id header that persists across reconnects (we'll honor that immediately). will add to support docs.

emily: putting this on priority and will update ACME with expected timeline: credit within 24-48h, patch and test early next week. leaving logs and reproduction steps here: curl repro below.

emily: ```bash
# repro (no buffering)
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "X-Stream-Id: stream-7f" \
  'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=psi-1' | sed -n '1,120p'
# mid-request, kill connection and immediately re-open with same X-Stream-Id to simulate blip
```

kevin: noted. thanks everyone. i'll post credit confirmation and invoice update here when done. :thumbsup:
